result.scientific_strategy:
## abd93958-a0b2-4d26-b212-96ebeb401d22 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The objective is at least 98% success, or 196 of 200 episodes, on the unchanged official two-joint-arm reach-and-hold task. Across twelve experiments and 72 development measurements, the fresh baseline reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.0% on the protected task-reference panel at checkpoint-100352, while full-radius transfer in experiment 2 reached 97.0% and 98.5% and remains the strongest measured artifact. Joint shaping, targeted sampling, unchanged continuation, hold-credit forfeiture, a lower transfer learning rate, sharper closeness shaping, doubled PPO rollout length, and temporal command smoothing did not improve that artifact; the two fresh replications instead remained at 62.5-67.5% on both development panels. The campaign therefore contains one useful transferred trajectory, poor fresh trajectories, and no robust cross-panel attainment. The retained policy's failures cluster near the 1 cm boundary, while fresh failures are broad; logged reward and proxy success repeatedly diverge from measured task success. Reward curvature, target exposure, rollout aggregation, and the tested low-pass execution change are weakened explanations under the tested transferred recipes, but action-level control and policy capacity remain unresolved. This provisional synthesis is campaign memory for reassessment and prescribes no next action.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, not logged reward or training success, is the policy-progress signal. Checkpoint and trajectory choice matter: several experiments showed proxy or late-training gains without task improvement. Full-radius transfer recovered two short-radius negative-angle failures from experiment 1, but experiment 2 still failed at roughly 9.4-9.9 cm and -123 to -128 degrees plus an 18.2 cm/-154.8 degree case. Detailed researcher-evaluation artifacts show that most retained-policy failures have maximum hold counts of zero or two steps and minimum distances close to the 1 cm boundary, whereas fresh failures are broad and often never approach the target. The current 11-value observation contains joint state, Cartesian error, both inverse-kinematics branch errors, direct two-joint actions, and saved normalization, so transfer is semantically compatible, not merely dimension-compatible. The lower learning rate preserved behavior but did not reduce residual count. In experiments 10 and 11, logged reward recovery and high proxy success did not establish measured task progress; experiment 11's endpoint had 0.97 logged success and 109.2 mean reward but only 97.0% researcher-panel and 97.5% task-reference success. Its task-reference failures remained near the 1 cm boundary and 500-step truncation, with later checkpoints adding negative-angle cases rather than removing the parent's residual set. Experiment 12 reached 97.0% on the researcher panel at all three measured checkpoints and 97.5%, then 98.5%, 98.5% on task-reference; its two later reference candidates had exactly the parent's three failing target cases, while the early candidate added two short-radius negative-angle failures. Training proxy success reached 1.00 at checkpoint-100352 and 115712, but measured task success did not improve. These findings are training/task discrepancies, not evidence of task progress. Fixed 200-episode panels are development evidence rather than the official final assessment. A transferred policy remains semantically compatible when its observation features and action coordinates are preserved; changing temporal command execution is nevertheless a behavioral intervention, not proof from tensor shape alone. The campaign has not isolated policy capacity from initialization variance: the successful trajectory used transfer, while experiments 5 and 6 used fresh 64x64 policies and were broadly weak.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether near-boundary failures are limited by action-level control or the learned policy class after reward-curvature, rollout-aggregation, and the tested temporal smoothing intervention failed to improve the retained trajectory. The smoothing result is limited to one transferred seed, one blend weight, three measured checkpoints, and the fixed development panels; it does not rule out other action-level controllers or execution changes. Transfer history and seed-dependent optimization remain confounded by the two poor fresh replications, and the effect of a larger policy class has not been observed. It is also unknown how well either development panel predicts the official final assessment. No open question is a prescribed next action.
